title: Treasury Note: Funding Personal Transfers and Early Release of ACH-Funded Principal
content:
The Personal Sender Account level in force at booking decides which funding methods a personal transfer may use: debit card, credit card, ACH bank debit, instant pay-by-bank, and inbound domestic wire, each permitted or not at that level. A delivery tier may narrow the funding methods further and never widens them.

## ACH-funded principal

A transfer funded by ACH bank debit is released to the payout partner before the debit settles only while the ACH-funded principal released early in the rolling 30 calendar days, including this transfer, stays within the level's early-release allowance in USD. Otherwise its principal waits the level's settlement wait in Paloma business days (Monday to Friday, excluding US Federal Reserve holidays) after booking before release, and that wait is built into its disclosed date of availability.

The rolling 30 calendar days covers transfers booked on the handling date or any of the 29 calendar days before it, and counts the principal of the customer's ACH-funded personal transfers in Bank Deposit, Cash Pickup and Mobile Wallet that were released before their ACH debit settled, leaving out transfers that are cancelled or refunded.

## Level changes

A level change applies to transfers booked after it and never re-releases or re-holds a transfer already booked.

## Worked check (hypothetical figures)

At Paloma Verified Plus the early-release allowance is 1500.00 USD and the settlement wait is 3 business days. A customer has had 1000.00 USD of ACH-funded principal released early in the rolling 30 calendar days.

| New ACH-funded transfer | Early-release total including it | Released before the debit settles? |
|---|---|---|
| 500.00 USD | 1500.00 USD | yes: it stays within 1500.00 |
| 600.00 USD | 1600.00 USD | no: the principal waits 3 Paloma business days after booking |
